question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,0]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-{y}^{2}+1 \\ {y}^{3}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,1]^{T}.$ Round your answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{1}≈[$ $-0.769$ $]$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-{y}^{2}+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-{y}^{2}+1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}-{x}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}-{x}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & -2y \\ -2x & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & -2y \\ -2x & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-{y}^{2}+1 \\ {y}^{3}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & -2y \\ -2x & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-{y}^{2}+1 \\ {y}^{3}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}3(-1)^{2} & -2(1) \\ -2(-1) & 3(1)^{2}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-1)^{3}-{1}^{2}+1 \\ {1}^{3}-(-1)^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{3\cdot 3-2\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{10}{13} \\ \frac{11}{13}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-0.769 \\ 0.846\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
